chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal from Isma'il ibn Mihran from al-Hasan ibn al-Hasan al-Marwazi from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman from Muhammad ibn Yahya, who said:

I was with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and he was asked: 'Is it added to the voluntary prayers in the month of Ramadan?' He said, 'Yes. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to pray after 'Isha' in his place of prayer, and he would prolong it. The people would gather behind him to pray with his prayer. When they became numerous behind him, he would leave them and enter his house. When the people dispersed, he would return to his place of prayer and pray as he used to pray. When the people became numerous behind him, he would leave them and enter his house. He used to do this repeatedly.'
ai.seo_question: What was the Prophet's method for leading voluntary night prayers in Ramadan according to Shia sources?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the Prophet’s (peace be upon him) modesty and strategic leadership during Taraweeh prayers, where he would prolong the prayer but withdraw to avoid burdening the community with obligatory status. This practice is historically significant as it informed the Caliph Umar’s decision to consolidate the prayer behind a single Imam, distinguishing it from the fragmented prayers of the Prophet’s era. It underscores the scholarly view that voluntary night prayers in Ramadan are highly recommended acts of devotion rather than fixed Sunnah Mu'akkadah.
